design: docs/DESIGN-house-rules.md §4 (the collision census that found it)
digest_algorithm: sha256 over the file's bytes with CRLF normalised to LF
what_this_records: This file exists for one reason: `prereg_pins.resolve_pin` follows a retirement to a SUCCESSOR pin, and three live rows pinning scripts/match_signatures.py retire into this commit. A retirement with nowhere to land is a pin deleted, which the walk refuses by design.

It preregisters no experiment and quotes no rate. It is a digest record, recorded in the same commit that changes the parser and before any artifact quotes a number measured through it — which is the whole content of the rule it is obeying.

the_change.what: match_signatures.Parser now accumulates a `rewrites` list: one record per big-operator capture, naming the authored token verbatim, the head it became, the characters discarded, the rule, and the token's position. ParsedNode carries it as `parse_rewrites`; build_report republishes it as a total top-level `parse_rewrites` section and on each twin-group member row that has one. An empty record is written nowhere.
the_change.why: The rewrite was lossy AND silent. Two person-authored identifiers collapsed to one tree with no trace, so a reader could not tell a well-formed big operator from a name the parser ate. The tree stays lossy — 17 committed templates depend on it — and stops being silent.

census.suffix_distribution: single-letter index names, 17 of 17; no prod_, max_ or min_ occurrence exists in the committed corpus
census.note: The suffixes being uniformly single-letter is recorded as a FACT, not used as a rule. A single-letter-versus-word heuristic would be a new authored judgement the design did not price; disclosure is total instead.

scope_verified_not_assumed.byte_identity: reports/signature_matches.json regenerates identical to the committed file after stripping the new disclosure, key for key. reports/specializations.json and reports/compression.json regenerate unchanged. Verified with scripts/check_report_regeneration.py.

frozen.why: The post-disclosure parser. Every chain that reached 26373234 now ends here, which is why one row carries three retirements: they all pin the same file for the same role.

non_claims: No refusal is claimed. `sum_total(x)` still parses, still becomes a sum, and still loses the word `total` from its tree; what changed is that the loss is now written down where a reader of the term's own receipt sees it.

No claim that the disclosure reaches every consumer of the parser. It reaches the parser object and the signature-matcher ledger that owns the hazard. A consumer that discards the parser instance discards the record, by construction.

This does not discharge H-P0's RESERVED_PREFIX guard and H-P0 does not discharge this. The guard converts the hazard at the declaration boundary; this lane converts it in the shipped parser. ROADMAP-v0.25 §2 orders this one first for exactly that reason.
No measurement is registered here and no floor is frozen.
evidence: tests/test_big_op_disclosure.py — the red-first test. Against the unmodified parser it ran 12 tests with 19 errors and 1 failure, the failure quoting a real committed term: `infotheory.entropy.shannon_entropy was rewritten with no record`.
